lines: DIRECTOR IN TOWN! DIRECTOR STILL IN TOWN! DIRECTOR —
...she's gone, actually. Went south an hour back and nobody thought to tell me.
I'll keep crying it until somebody official says stop. That's the job.
FOUR ROADS! WEST TO THE QUARRY, SOUTH TO THE COAST, NORTH TO NOTHING!
EAST ROAD STILL CLOSED! THIRTY-ONE YEARS AND COUNTING!
...Sorry. Force of habit. You shout for a living, you stop being able to stop.
There is a lad been sat on the ridge milestone since dawn with a slate, counting carts.
I asked him why. He said somebody had to, and offered me his tea.
Change your team here or do not go up at all. That is not advice, that is the paddock rule.
A team that goes up the ridge tired does not come down it.
And it is worse than it was, because you cannot get up it now without stopping for somebody.
You went in and you came out again. Most people manage one of those.
She'll have been reasonable with you. She's always reasonable.
Nine years I've worked for her and I still can't say if that's a comfort.
Office is open. Ask us whatever you like, we're instructed to answer.
That isn't generosity, it's policy. We have nothing to hide.
And we are very, very tired of being asked.
I am going to work for the Foundation.
They get a coat and a brass thing and everyone stops talking when they walk in.
Mum says that is not a reason. It is a bit of a reason.
You met her, then. Everyone says the same thing afterwards.
That she was reasonable. Always that word. Never once anything else.
I've a letter to carry back to Sorrell and I don't know what to put in it.
You're the one Sorrell sent out? He writes to this office every week.
They keep the letters. Filed, dated, never answered. I've seen the drawer.
Go in and look for yourself. The Director came down herself two days ago.
Walked up from Tideglass. Two days on the coast road and not one gull the whole way.
I have made that walk since I was nine. There are always gulls.
You do not notice a sound until you have spent two days listening for it.

tr_shop_hand: Net Vessels are new in. Good on anything that swims.
Which is most of what you'll meet south of here, so don't be clever about it.

lines: The Director spoke to you personally. That doesn't happen.
I've filed everything she said. I've read it back twice since.
It's all correct. Every line. I'd feel better if one bit of it weren't.
Survey office. Soundings, bearings, permits. In that order, please.
No, you may not see the west face readings. Yes, I know how that sounds.
It isn't bad. It's procedure. Those are different, and I'm required to say so.

tr_concord_hand: Nine sites this season and not one of them near the coast.
You'd think a body that worries about the sea might survey the sea.
...I've said too much. I say that a lot lately, and I keep on saying things.

lines: It went back off the well on Thursday. I went down and looked and it was off the well.
Eighty-one years of waiting to be wrong, and I was right, and it has passed, and I am still here.
Sit with me a minute. I still do not want anything. It is just a better minute than the last one.
It is past the well. It was at the well on Tuesday and this morning it is in the tannery yard.
The south road has not flooded. It has gone. There is no road there now, there is a channel.
You came in from somewhere. Tell me which way, and then go back out of it while it is still there.
I was ten at the last Turning and I have been waiting eighty-one years to be wrong about it.
It is at the well. I went down and looked this morning and it is at the well.
Sit with me a minute. I do not want anything. I would just rather not be on my own.
You've been in to see the Kerrow girl. Her brother's name was Ald.
Nobody says it now. They say two hundred and forty, which is worse.
Decide what you like about her. Decide it knowing she isn't pretending.
Eighty-one years at this crossroads and six of them spent indoors.
I remember the last Turning. I was ten. The sea came up the south road to the well.
Everyone talks about stopping it now as though that's a simple thing. It isn't.
But nobody who was there thinks it should be allowed to happen twice.
Loud lad sat here yesterday and gave me a count off a slate. Fourteen carts.
That is the best news anyone has brought this table in a month, and he would not take a plate for it.
I have put his fourteen in the book anyway. He will be back.
Sit. Eat. The only rent on that bench is telling me what you saw on the road.
Four hundred years we have done it that way. A village that cannot see round the corner
buys its warnings a plate at a time, and it has never once been a bad bargain.
The wind stopped. Four days ago, in an afternoon, and the hollow is still air again.
I have hung the hides back up and then I stood underneath them for a long time.
Four hundred years. I very nearly broke it. I did not break it.
There is wind in the hollow. There has never been wind in the hollow.
Four hundred years of hides hung in still air and I took the lot down yesterday.
You cannot argue with it and you cannot move a village. So I took the hides down.
Salt on the wind and no wind in the hollow. That is the whole trick and you cannot fake it.
Tideglass has the salt and no shelter. The ridge has the shelter and no salt.
Here has both. Four hundred years of hides, and the smell is the rent.
Fire is out. Not blown out. The nine of us let it out, together, on Thursday morning.
We burned a winter of wood in six days and the parish has already carted us a winter of wood.
That man is not coming back. Somebody read us what he wrote. We would still have said no.
It went out at two. Nine of us on that ridge and it went out at two in the morning.
We had it back by first light. Wet wood, so it smokes, and from out at sea it will look like nothing at all.
So there is a light and there is not a light. I have not worked out which one to say in the village.
Nine of us on the rota and there are four up there now, day and night, keeping it in.
The wind takes it flat and then it comes back. We have burned a winter of wood in six days.
That man with the machine can come back if he likes. We will still say no. We will just say it tired.
Up the ridge at dusk, light it, down again in the dark. Nine of us on the rota.
Salthollow has kept that light since before Salthollow had a name.
Somebody came last month and offered to do it for us. With a machine. We said no.
Sixteen days. Down and back, down and back, and the wage comes every Friday in coin.
They never say what is in them. I have stopped hearing myself not ask.
Do not tell me. If you find out, do not tell me. I have three at home.
Best-paid work on this coast and all you do is walk. I would take it again tomorrow.
My husband has been up on that ridge since yesterday with a broken axle.
The Foundation came out, counted his load, wrote it in a book and went away.
Nobody counted him.
I rang it once more and everybody came out again, and this time I told them why before they asked.
Three reasons on the board and a fourth underneath in pencil, in my hand.
Somebody will make that permanent after I am gone. I am not going to be the one who does it.
I rang it at six and eleven people came out.
Fire, wreck, beacon, weather. Four reasons on that board and not one of them covers an empty street.
I am going to keep ringing it. Somebody up on the ridge road might hear it and know which way the village is.
I rang it for weather. There is no reason on the board for weather.
Four hundred years of that rope and I am the one who made up a fourth reason.
Everybody came out. Nobody asked me which it was. That is what has stayed with me.
Fire, wreck, or the beacon wanting wood. Three reasons and no others, ever.
Four rings this year. Three of them were the beacon.
The fourth was a fortnight ago. Nobody has told me yet what that one was for.

_note: TARIN: the ledger in src/systems/tarin.ts publishes tarin_at_<beat> as a flag, and these variants are how the town talks about him between the times he is on screen. They are copies of the shared voices in data/dialogue/common.json (tarin_word_street, _hall, _clinic, _shop) because nothing on any map points an NPC at those ids yet -- if you would rather have the shared ones, set an NPC script to tarin_word_street and delete the copy here. First match wins, so they sit at the top and the ungated line still ends every list. The tr_crier speaker name was left behind when the village map dropped that NPC, which fails tests/content.test.js; the name is gone and the entry is kept, so re-placing an NPC with that id is one line.
